newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond spreads firm as Treas rallies.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond spreads firm as Treas rallies.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds held pace with big gains in U.S. Treasuries and spreads were mostly unchanged, while opportunity knocked for several finance related issuers, traders said.
But corporate bond buying was still termed light to moderate as the masses of investors remained cautious ahead of the release of potent manufacturing data on Thursday and April jobs data on Friday.
"People want a little more confirmation that this rally is for real," one high-grade industrials trader said. "But all the signs should lend support to the corporate market."

Treasuries ran sharply higher following reports that said the employment cost index rose just 0.6 percent in the first quarter compared with an expected 0.9 percent rise and a 3.0 percent drop in orders for durable goods in March.
The 30-year bond closed up 49/32 to yield 6.98 percent.

High-grade corporate buyers were also sidelined ahead of the $2.0 billion CSX Corp multi-tranche offering via a Salomon Brothers led syndicate, traders said. The deal may be priced on Thursday, according to market sources.

Back to Tuesday's action, issues included $150 million 7.20 percent 10-year notes from Norwest Financial Inc priced at a 48 basis points spread; $100 million 6.70 percent three-year notes from CIT Group Holdings Inc priced at a 26 basis point spread; $100 million 7.125 percent five-year notes from FINOVA Capital Corp priced at 51 basis points over; and $200 million 30-year capital securities from Dime Capital Trust I priced to yield 230 basis points over the curve.
Also, American Stores sold $100 million 20-year 7.90 percent debentures at 85 basis points over and $200 million 40put12 7.50 percent debt priced at 75 basis points over.

Turning to high-yields, prices were bid higher by 1/2 point on average with some rising even more when the stock market surged. The Dow closed up 179 points, its unofficial second-largest daily point rise.
"Trading was not unusually brisk but everybody was forced to take a second look with stocks way up," a trader said.

Traders and analysts pointed to some better activity for competitive local exchange carriers and satellite concerns -- Teleport Communication cash pay bonds were stronger by 3/4 point following a positive cash flow report.
Lenfest Communications' 9-3/8 percent debt outperformed the field by gaining one point to 95-1/4 bid near the close, according to one trader.

Better bidding in high-grades was seen for Tele-Communications Inc paper ahead of an analysts meeting on Wednesday, traders said. On the flip side, Tobacco paper continued to slide -- Philip Morris paper widened as much as five basis points, they said.
